USBKill turns thumb drives into computer kill switches

I'm curious if one of these three things, will this device work on?

  1. The USB drive is not in the order of boot in the BOIS.
  2. The computer does not recognize any USB slots as a valid drive through third-party software.
  3. The USB drive is disabled by default in the BIOS or has something physically jammed in the slot.
  4. All external drives are monitored through the network, and if any is found to have unauthorized access, they are terminated through a "soft-kill" switch.
  5. The computer maybe infected with a virus / worm / script to infect all USB drives that connect to it. Or Some entity is using a man-in-the-middle attack to access the computer; and thus, your device.

Not all of these may even apply, but I've had at least one of these happen to me at a public library. They are not always monitored for viruses or cleaned. And any filtering software / anti-virus software may have the option to disable USB drives when needed. Great idea nonetheless. ^.^

In the case of using the actual library computers, one of those variables may interfere. This script is more oriented towards your own machine. It queries the usb slots on a hardware level seeking a change and issues a shutdown command when said change is found.
